t: Marx and Engels held that a society’s mode of production is the base of its politics, law and ideas, and that class struggle drives historical change.

Marxism divided into many schools after Marx’s death; the most prominent in the 20th century was Marxism–Leninism, the official ideology of the Soviet Union and other Marxist states, while Western Marxism, libertarian Marxism and Marxist humanism often criticised state socialism.

Critics from several quarters, among them Karl Popper, Austrian economists and anarchists, attacked its predictions, its economics and its view of the state, while its concepts of alienation, exploitation and class struggle entered the social sciences and humanities.
dyk: Engels did not favour the word Marxism, and in 1882 he reported that Marx had said of the views of Paul Lafargue, a self-proclaimed Marxist, that if they were Marxist, then “one thing is certain and that is that I am not a Marxist.”
ev: Marx sets out the materialist conception of history in The German Ideology
Marx and Engels publish the 12,000-word Communist Manifesto in February
Engels publishes Origins of the Family, Private Property, and the State after Marx’s death in 1883
The Bolsheviks take power from the Russian Provisional Government in the October Revolution
Marx’s Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844 appear, the birth of Marxist humanism
The People’s Republic of China is declared after the Chinese Communist Revolution
The Cuban Revolution brings Fidel Castro to power; he later adopts the Leninist model
The Soviet Union dissolves, and its constituent nations abandon Marxist–Leninist models

f.thinkers: Karl Marx and Friedrich Engels, who co-developed communist theory; Karl Kautsky, who popularised the term Marxism; Eduard Bernstein, his revisionist rival; Vladimir Lenin; Rosa Luxemburg; Leon Trotsky; Joseph Stalin; Mao Zedong; Louis Althusser; Leszek Kołakowski, a critic
f.texts: The German Ideology (1845); Theses on Feuerbach (1845); The Communist Manifesto (1848); A Contribution to the Critique of Political Economy (1859); Capital; Engels’s The Condition of the Working Class in England in 1844 and Origins of the Family, Private Property, and the State (1884); Marx’s Economic and Philosophic Manuscripts of 1844, published in 1932
f.ideas: historical materialism; base and superstructure; class struggle as the force of historical change; exploitation through surplus value; alienation; class consciousness; revolution replacing capitalism with socialism and then a classless, stateless and moneyless society
f.today: China, Cuba, Laos, North Korea and Vietnam remained the only officially Marxist–Leninist states at the turn of the 21st century; Marxist theory continues to be developed by thinkers such as David Harvey, Nancy Fraser and Silvia Federici, and shapes many academic fields
